criteria.description: Correctly identifies the manipulation-model/constraints category with reasoning.

solutions.fullSolution: Manipulation model (state/observations -> constraints): the output is a spatial success constraint (grasp pose), not a control, value, or plan, matching RLEARN-06's grasp/affordance model row.
Simulation/domain transfer, specifically domain randomization: all data comes from a physics engine with randomized parameters, not the real robot or a human, matching RLEARN-04.

criteria.description: Correctly identifies inverse dynamics as the shortcut target.
Correctly explains why Q avoids the extra dynamics-model step V requires.

solutions.fullSolution: Learning Q(s,a) directly shortcuts the need for DYN-01's inverse dynamics model (qddot -> u). With only V(s), converting 'which direction increases value' into an actual control needs a differentiable dynamics model; Q already scores actions directly, no separate dynamics-model conversion step needed.

criteria.description: Correctly explains the Jacobian discontinuity at contact onset.
Correctly connects this to MANIP-02's hybrid dynamics framing.

solutions.fullSolution: Objects are part of the multibody system but not articulated: untouched, their Jacobian w.r.t. robot joints is exactly zero, jumping discontinuously the instant contact occurs. This hard on/off switching is exactly MANIP-02's hybrid dynamical system idea (there, stance/swing phase switching in legged locomotion): smooth continuous dynamics interleaved with discrete, non-smooth events, breaking the purely-continuous DYN-01 through DYN-04 framework.
